title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's notes for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The neighbouring pages in the scan are unrelated: they are typed pages of SGA 7 IX (Néron models, Barsotti–Tate groups) and give no context here.

Setting. Grothendieck has a construction A_*(S, S^+, t) attached to:
- a pd-ring S,
- a pd-ideal S^+,
- an element t of S^+.
Its values are graded, filtered, differential (co)simplicial algebras; the transcription reads 'différentielle à simpliciale'.

Functoriality. A pd-morphism u : (S,S^+) → (S',S'^+) with u(t) = λ t' induces a map A_*(S,S^+,t) → A_*(S',S'^+,t'), and that map a priori depends on λ. If t' is a regular element (a non-zero-divisor; the manuscript word is probably 'régulier', not 'singulier'), λ is uniquely determined by u. So A_* becomes a genuine functor on the category of triples with t regular and morphisms satisfying u(t) ∈ S·t'.

Universal example. The condition holds for S = k{T} (the divided-power polynomial algebra), S^+ = (T)_pd, t = T, when k is torsion-free. Grothendieck sets A_*(k) := A_*(k{T}, (T)_pd, T) and wants its endomorphisms as a bare differential (co)simplicial k-algebra. He deliberately forgets the S-algebra structure, the grading, the divided powers and the filtration.

The monoid G_k. Since k{T} is the free pd-algebra on T, a pd-endomorphism u is determined by u(T). Requiring u(T) = λ(T)·T identifies G_k with the set S = k{T}, given a twisted multiplication from composition. Writing u_λ for T ↦ λ(T)T, one gets u_{λ'}(u_λ(T)) = λ(λ'(T)T)·λ'(T)·T, so λ'*λ = λ'(T)·λ(λ'(T)T). Grothendieck then writes u_λ u_{λ'} = u_{λλ'} for this product.

Injectivity. λ ↦ (u_λ)_* is an injective monoid homomorphism into End(A_*(k)). Already its degree-1 part is injective, because A_1(k) ≅ k{T}{X_0} and (u_λ)_*(X_0) = λ X_0.

Where the page breaks off. He introduces:
- H_k, the monoid of G_k-equivariant endomorphisms of A_*(k);
- Ω_k, the monoid of all endomorphisms.
The page stops just before stating their relation, presumably a computation of Ω_k in terms of G_k and H_k, i.e. the 'symmetries' of the universal pd de Rham object.

Purpose. Pin down the natural operations or symmetries of a universal pd-de Rham type construction by computing the endomorphism monoid of its value on the universal pd-line.
errors: The composition formula as transcribed, λ'{T}λ{T}λ'{λ}, does not match a direct computation. Composition gives (u_{λ'}∘u_λ)(T) = λ(λ'(T)T)·λ'(T)·T, so the product must involve λ evaluated at λ'(T)T (or the reverse, depending on convention). This is either a slip or a misreading of the handwriting.
'u_λ u_{λ'} = u_{λλ'}' must be read with the twisted product λ*λ', not ordinary multiplication in k{T}.
Evaluating λ ∈ k{T} at λ'(T)T needs λ'(T)T in a pd-ideal. That holds because it lies in (T)_pd, but the point is left implicit.

ideas.what: Functoriality of a pd-de Rham type construction A_*(S,S^+,t) restricted to triples with t a non-zero-divisor, so that the scaling factor λ is unique
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of a functor on pd-rings with a marked element
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; part of standard crystalline/pd-algebra technique (Berthelot, Illusie)

ideas.what: Monoid of pd-substitutions T ↦ λ(T)T of the divided-power line k{T}, under composition
ideas.modern_name: pd (sharp) analogue of the monoid of formal coordinate changes fixing the origin; related to the actions of G_m^♯ / G_a^♯ on de Rham-type objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: G_m^♯ and G_a^♯ symmetries of de Rham/Hodge structures: Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie (2020s)

ideas.what: Computing the endomorphism monoid (all endomorphisms vs. G_k-equivariant ones) of the universal object A_*(k)
ideas.modern_name: natural operations / symmetries of the (pd) de Rham complex

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to compute the endomorphism monoid Ω_k of the universal pd-de Rham object over the divided-power line. He compares it with the G_k-equivariant endomorphisms H_k, where G_k is the monoid of pd-substitutions T ↦ λ(T)T. This page does not finish the computation.
missed.quote: si H_k est le monoïde des G_k-endomorphismes de la k-algèbre différentielle à simpliciale A_*(k), et Ω_k le monoïde de tous les endomorphismes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work describes the symmetries of de Rham/Hodge-filtered cohomology through groups such as G_m^♯ and G_a^♯ (Drinfeld, Bhatt–Lurie). A 1976 attempt to compute the symmetries of a universal pd-de Rham object via pd-substitutions on k{T} may anticipate that viewpoint. Whether it really does depends on the following pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, technical step in the 1976 pd-de Rham lecture notes: a monoid of pd-substitutions acting on a universal object, aimed at determining its endomorphisms. It is suggestive of later sharp-group symmetries of de Rham cohomology, but the page itself is routine bookkeeping and incomplete.
transcription_corrections: 'élément singulier' is likely 'élément régulier' (non-zero-divisor); this is needed for λ to be uniquely determined.
'La condition [?] singulière' is likely 'La condition imposée sur (S,S^+_pd,t)' or 'condition de régularité'.
'différentielle à simpliciale' may be 'différentielle cosimpliciale' (or 'simpliciale'); the handwriting is ambiguous.
The struck/inserted target category reads 'anneaux gradués (différentiels) filtrés', i.e. graded differential filtered rings.
The neighbouring-page transcriptions (SGA 7 IX, Néron models) are from a different document and give no context for this page.
